> I have no idea how to solve that check for [GHA / 🐧 Linux / Editor w/ Mono (target=editor)

You need to bind the `SoftBodyForm` enum entries, as well as the new `PhysicsServer3D` methods, in `PhysicsServer3D::_bind_methods`, then generate the documentation "skeleton" by running Godot with `--doctool`.

EDIT: You'll need to bind the new methods in `PhysicsServer3DExtension::_bind_methods` as well.

I'm pretty sure I bound everything that needed to be bound in `PhysicsServer3D` and `PhysicsServer3DExtension`.

I just ran `godot --doctool` and it changed about 100 files.  I don't think you want me to check all of this in.  How exactly am I meant to use it?

> I'm pretty sure I bound everything that needed to be bound in `PhysicsServer3D` and `PhysicsServer3DExtension`.

No, there's unfortunately even more boilerplate needed. See [these changes](https://github.com/blackears/godot/compare/volumetric_soft_body...mihe:godot:volumetric_soft_body) (patch [here](https://github.com/blackears/godot/compare/volumetric_soft_body...mihe:godot:volumetric_soft_body.patch)), which also include the output from `--doctool`.

> I just ran `godot --doctool` and it changed about 100 files. I don't think you want me to check all of this in. How exactly am I meant to use it?

That should not happen. `--doctool` will remove all of the class reference XML files and regenerate them, so a lot of files will technically be touched, but the resulting modified files should be limited to only the bindings you changed. Was there any error of some sort perhaps, that caused it to not regenerate them after deletion? Does it work better if you incorporate the changes I linked above?
Thanks for the patch. I think part of the problem is that I ran doctool with Godot 4.5.1 earlier. I tried again with Godot 4.6.1 and got fewer changes, but still quite a few of them:

> I tried again with Godot 4.6.1 and got fewer changes, but still quite a few of them

You need to run `--doctool` with your local Godot build, i.e. the one with all these changes in it, not with any of the official builds. Sorry, I should have made that clearer.

EDIT: I don't know if the working directory matters, but running it from the root of your local clone is probably best.

That's a much better fit.  However, the changes `--doctool` is making now is just deleting the documentation I added to PhysicsServer3D.xml and PhysicsServer3DExtension.xml.  Was I supposed to put this somewhere else so that it would generate these entries?

> However, the changes it is making now is just deleting the documentation I added to PhysicsServer3D.xml and PhysicsServer3DExtension.xml

If you ran it without discarding the changes that the previous `--doctool` runs made, then it can end up deleting some documentation, since it carries some stuff over from the files that are already on disk. So I'm guessing the descriptions and stuff were deleted, since those methods/enums didn't exist in those earlier builds you ran with `--doctool`.

Just discard all your local changes in the `doc` folder and run it again (with the changes you brought over from my branch) and you should hopefully find that it results in no modified files.

> Was I supposed to put this somewhere else so that it would generate these entries?

Whenever you change anything with the bindings you'll want to run `--doctool` after you've done so, to generate the XML entries for any new classes/methods/properties/enums, and then you can fill in the descriptions in the actual XML files. So you don't have to write the XML tags and stuff yourself.

So in this case you'll still want to add a description for the `soft_body_form` property in the `SoftBody3D` XML I guess, since I didn't write any for you.

I reverted all changes I made, which gives me the `PhysicsServer3D.xml` and `PhysicsServer3DExtension.xml` files as they're currently checked in, with the documentation.  However, when I run `.\bin\godot.windows.editor.dev.x86_64.exe --doctool`, it regenerates these documents with the entries for the methods I added stripped out.  I'm running the doctool in the project directory, if that matters.

> However, when I run `.\bin\godot.windows.editor.dev.x86_64.exe --doctool`, it regenerates these documents with the entries for the methods I added stripped out.

Did you build after you pulled in my changes? Make sure you do so with `dev_build=yes` as well, since you're running the `*.dev.*` binary.

I rebuild the project with `scons platform=windows dev_build=yes vsproj=yes`, then ran `.\bin\godot.windows.editor.dev.x86_64.exe --doctool`.  Entries for `soft_body_get_form` are just not appearing in the generated docs for `PhysicsServer3D.xml` and `PhysicsServer3DExtension.xml`.  

At the moment, the only differences between my code tree and this PR are the two generated xml files.

> I rebuild the project with `scons platform=windows dev_build=yes vsproj=yes`

Just to clarify, did you build from Visual Studio after running this command? When you pass `vsproj=yes` you won't actually build anything, it will only generate the Visual Studio solution, despite what the command-line output might (confusingly) suggest with its `Building for platform [...]` message.

Okay, after building project again in Visual Studio, doctool is now generating the documentation stubs.  Can I just hand edit those to put the descriptions back in?  

Also, after adding the description text back in, I end up with something identical to what is already checked in.  The only difference is I now have a newly generated PhysicsServer3D.xml.bak file.  Does that need to be checked in?

>  Can I just hand edit those to put the descriptions back in?

Yes, or you just discard any local changes to the `doc` folder and run `--doctool` again. The only reason the descriptions were discarded was because of the previous "invalid" runs of `--doctool`, which prevented it from preserving the descriptions when regenerating everything.

> Also, after adding the description text back in, I end up with something identical to what is already checked in.

Yes, as I mentioned above, I included the `--doctool` output in the change you merged in, so you should end up with no changes. You still need to add a description to the `soft_body_form` property stub that my change brought in though.

> The only difference is I now have a newly generated PhysicsServer3D.xml.bak file. Does that need to be checked in?

`*.bak` files is not something Godot emits, as far as I know. I'm guessing you were using Notepad++ to edit the XML files perhaps?

You're right about the `.bak` file. I'll just delete it.

I don't see a stub for the property `soft_body_form`.  Just the getter and setter methods.  At least a search for `soft_body_form` in `PhysicsServer3D.xml` and `PhysicsServer3DExtension.xml` is turning up nothing.

> I don't see a stub for the property `soft_body_form`. Just the getter and setter methods. At least a search for `soft_body_form` in `PhysicsServer3D.xml` and `PhysicsServer3DExtension.xml` is turning up nothing.

It's for the `SoftBody3D` property that you added, so it's in `SoftBody3D.xml`.

Okay, I think that's done now.  

That's a lot to remember.  Is there any checklist to follow if I need to add another method or property later?

> That's a lot to remember. Is there any checklist to follow if I need to add another method or property later?

Not that I'm aware of, no. The physics server interface is one of the more boilerplate-heavy parts of the codebase, but it doesn't change all that often, so there hasn't been any dire need to documenting it or cleaning it up.

As for properties/methods on scene nodes, like `SoftBody3D` in this case, everything starts in `SomeClassNameHere::_bind_methods` and flows out from there. It's hard to mess anything up too badly. The CI jobs should catch any missed `--doctool` and such.

The simulation does blow up a bit in some situations.  My contribution is about building the tetrahedral structure.  I'd need someone who understand the physics better to advise on how to set the physics parameters properly.

The delay is probably because it seems that the editor calls `JoltSoftBody3D::_create_shared_settings()` twice when you switch to it in the editor.  It's fast enough on my machine, but maybe it's a bit slow on others.  Maybe that could be skipped if I detect the editor is running?  Or could that affect @tool scripts?

I think the tetrahedralization is pretty robust.  It relies on the existing `Geometry3D::tetrahedralize_delaunay` to do the tricky work of building the tetrahedra.  I could look into adding Steiner points which may make the simulation more stable by breaking up the bigger tetrahedra and reducing the number of slivers.

I say switch back to `auto` for the lambdas, or move them to be functions in the anonymous namespace at the top of the file instead. It doesn't look like they capture anything anyway, despite the `[&]` capture clause. Just the added compile times from `<functional>` alone makes it quite overkill here, in my opinion.

![unstable_sim](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7867be36-0682-4ac1-9044-20b6ea873d95)

I'm increasingly thinking that it may be a good idea to rewrite the whole tetrahedralization algorithm.  Geometry3D::tetrahedralize_delaunay seems like a simple implementation of the Bowyer-Watson algorithm, and one that doesn't handle points that lie on circumsphere boundaries robustly.  It also doesn't guarantee it will follow the input geometry, and it produces tetrahedralizations with a lot of slivers.  Replacing it, though, will be a lot of work.
